description: Risk belongs to the dependency, not the repository, so both gates carry this part. Dependencies that never ship merge themselves in a branch of their own even where a person merges the rest; dependencies on the always-review list wait for a dashboard tick even where CI merges the rest. Majors keep the tick, security fixes and Webgrip’s own packages keep their own rules, which come later.

packageRules.description: Always review: libraries that hold credentials, sign or verify tokens, or speak to the database. A green test suite rarely covers a changed token check or connection default, so their minor, patch and digest updates wait for a dashboard tick in a branch of their own, whatever the gate. The tick is their gate, so they carry no soak: a tick on an update still inside its soak is discarded. Only where they ship: as a devDependency or require-dev they fall to the never-ships rules below. The list is the owner’s to set (ADR 0001); it starts with what Webgrip code uses today, such as webgrip/ploeg’s golang-jwt, pgx and lib/pq.

Never ships: npm devDependencies and Composer require-dev, which is where linters, formatters, test runners and type packages live. They are not installed in what a repository deploys, so a green CI run is the whole question; their minor, patch and pin updates share a branch of their own that merges itself after the soak, apart from the branch a person merges. A database driver used only by tests is one of them: the always-review rule excludes these dependency types.
Never ships: type packages carry no runtime code, whichever dependency list they sit in.
